paper.one_line_finding: Human Creativity and Copilot exceeded Human Confirmation in adjusted overall story quality by 0.3376 (SE 0.106) and 0.3158 (SE 0.105), respectively (both p < 0.01; PDF p. 51, Table S7), while semantic similarity was 0.710, 0.743, and 0.779, respectively (PDF p. 7).
paper.shared_samples: No overlap with another paper is stated. S1's writing days use the same cohort; S2 reuses its baseline DAT scores, with no new human recruitment. Do not add S2's count to S1 or treat them as independent human samples.

studies.label: Two-day classroom creative-writing experiment

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 18 (printed SI p. 2), A.1, Participants
counts_source.quote: A total of 285 students successfully participated in the experiment.

arms.name: Human Confirmation
arms.description: Day 2: ChatGPT handles ideation, outlining, drafting, and editing. Students prompt, evaluate, accept/reject, and request regeneration but may not supply their own ideas.

arms.name: Human Creativity
arms.description: Day 2: students ideate and outline without AI; ChatGPT drafts and edits. Students prompt and accept/reject generated text but may not add new ideas during production.

arms.name: Copilot
arms.description: Day 2: students and ChatGPT collaborate iteratively throughout ideation, outlining, drafting, and editing; students can write, edit, and supply ideas.

arms.name: Writing without AI (Day 1)
arms.description: Shared earlier session: every student writes manually before the AI session. This is a fixed-order baseline, not a separately randomized control arm, and is not used in extracted contrasts.

studies.task: Students in an elective emerging-technologies course write a new 1,000-word short story of any genre on each study day, following ideation, outlining, drafting, and editing stages.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT 3.5
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 4, Experimental Design; PDF p. 8, Discussion. Model release year is not printed.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is stated in the manuscript or included Supporting Information.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Overall effectiveness in conveying the main ideas creatively, interestingly, coherently, and with good writing; seven-point scale from extremely bad to extremely good. Four ratings per story: two fellow participants and two external student research assistants, blinded to author and treatment; PDF p. 19 (printed SI p. 3), Evaluation, and PDF p. 41 (printed SI p. 25), B.4.

sources.locator: PDF p. 5, Results, Writing Quality, comparison of Human Creativity with Copilot
sources.quote: No significant differences emerged between the latter two groups.

estimates.notes: The paper states that these two groups did not differ significantly but prints no pairwise coefficient, SE, test statistic, or exact p-value. Table S7 estimates each group against Human Confirmation. No subtraction of coefficients or derivation of the pairwise uncertainty was performed. Evaluation-level regression; the paper does not state participant/story clustering, evaluator effects, or the variance estimator (PDF p. 23, printed SI p. 7). Arm-specific people counts, regression observation counts, and arm SDs are unreported. Figure 2 plots arm means and intervals without text-layer numerical values; none is read from the figure. Table 1 pools ratings across days and arms and cannot supply an arm-specific SD.

estimates.primary_override_reason: Rule 5: The paper explicitly names the covariate-adjusted regression as primary, excluding the two unadjusted robustness candidates under rule 1. Of the remaining contrasts with Human Confirmation as the paper's shared reference, rule 5 favors Copilot because it permits participants to initiate tasks or seek AI input at any stage. (PDF p. 44 (SI p. 28), C.2, Main Findings Regarding Performance; PDF p. 51 (SI p. 35), Table S7 note; PDF p. 19 (SI p. 3), A.1, Copilot definition.: "The primary regression model accounts for individual characteristics, [...] the Human Confirmation group is set as the baseline. [...] Participants could initiate tasks independently or request AI input or feedback at any stage.")

estimates.outcome: Semantic similarity between different writers' stories
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Cosine similarity of each final story's OpenAI text-embedding-3-large embedding to the average embedding of the other stories in its condition (PDF p. 16, Figure 4C caption). Each writer submits one final story on Day 2. Higher values mean more similar stories across writers.

sources.locator: PDF p. 7, Content Diversity, Human Creativity arm
PDF p. 7, Content Diversity, Copilot arm

estimates.notes: Both intervals are confidence intervals for arm means, not for the between-arm difference. The control interval is preserved in control_ci_lower/control_ci_upper/control_ci_level. No arm SD, exact between-arm test, numerical p-value, or contrast confidence interval is printed; none is derived. Contrast-specific people and output counts are unreported. The pooled corpus size across all days and arms is not used as the N for this comparison. The point-score unit is one story, but the paper does not specify how the intervals were calculated or whether they account for dependence created by comparison with the shared group mean. The uncertainty basis is therefore unclear. Raw cosine similarity values and signs are retained. The text calls the ordered semantic-similarity differences statistically significant without giving pairwise test statistics or p-values. open_items: Exact randomized and unique analyzed people totals, people per AI arm, and regression-specific people/observation counts are not printed. The cohort count is not relabeled as an exact randomized or analyzed count, and stories/ratings are not relabeled as people (PDF pp. 18-21, printed SI pp. 2-5).

Quality regressions are evaluation-level. The paper does not specify the SE estimator or adjustment for multiple ratings per writer/story (PDF p. 23, printed SI p. 7; Tables S4 and S7). Participant-level precision remains unavailable.

No treatment/control SDs or participant-level quality SDs are printed. Table 1 pools ratings across AI arms and the no-AI day. Exact quality arm means and CIs are only plotted in Figure 2 and are not read from the figure.

For semantic and genre similarity, the CI and test procedures and handling of shared group-reference dependence are not stated; exact pairwise tests and pairwise confidence intervals are not printed (PDF pp. 6-7, 15-16).
For number of genres per story, the arm CIs are printed but their construction, arm counts, SDs, and pairwise tests are not supplied (PDF p. 6).

The exact overall-quality contrast between Human Creativity and Copilot is not printed. The text reports no significant difference; no coefficient difference or uncertainty is derived under the transcription-only rule (PDF pp. 5, 51).

The binary-genre-vector cosine measure has no exact value in the Atlas measure vocabulary. Following the reconciled form, S1-O7.measure is null; the scoring method is nevertheless specified (PDF p. 16).
The model release year is not stated; ai_tool.year remains null. The document has no printed version/date, although its hash matches the citation record identifying arXiv v2.

Task duration is internally inconsistent: the main text and recruitment section specify 105 minutes; SI day-specific task descriptions specify 75 minutes. The calendar interval between sessions is not given (PDF pp. 4, 18-20).
Genre-composition values are available only in Figure 4A; numeric fields remain null under the figure-only rule. This descriptive vector has no single signed scalar effect (PDF pp. 15-16).

review_corrections.basis: 'A total of 285 students successfully participated in the experiment.' (PDF p. 18, printed SI p. 2, A.1 Participants; also PDF p. 4). Students were randomized to the three AI conditions on Day 2; no analyzed total is printed (271 Day-2 stories are reported on PDF p. 21, one per writer, but as a count of stories).
